title: Azure Blob multipart upload delegation-key request: only 403 AuthorizationPermissionMismatch falls back to proxied upload, other Azure errors propagate
answers: Why did my Azure artifact upload silently go through the MLflow proxy instead of showing an authentication error?
Which Azure errors make a multipart artifact upload fall back to proxied upload?
Azure 403 AuthorizationFailure when logging artifacts with DefaultAzureCredential: where is it handled?
Where does MLflow request the user delegation key for Azure artifact uploads?
body:
Path: The user-delegation-key request inside Azure Blob multipart upload setup, which runs when a token-credential client uploads an artifact in blocks. The chokepoint is mlflow/store/artifact/azure_blob_artifact_repo.py:AzureBlobArtifactRepository.create_multipart_upload, where HttpResponseError from get_user_delegation_key is classified and then either converted to the fallback exception or re-raised.
Rule: Convert an azure.core HttpResponseError into _UnsupportedMultipartUploadException (raised `from e`) only when status_code == 403 and error_code == "AuthorizationPermissionMismatch", which is the RBAC case where the identity lacks permission to request a delegation key. Re-raise every other HttpResponseError unchanged. Do not match on status code alone: Azure also returns 403 for AuthenticationFailed and AuthorizationFailure, and a broad match hides those failures behind the proxy fallback.
Symptom: Before the fix, a broad 403 match would have converted authentication, account, and network-policy failures into the proxied-upload fallback, so the upload would proceed through the proxy and the real Azure error would never reach the user.
Constraints: Throttling (429), transient Azure failures, and authentication failures must still propagate to the caller. The fallback exception is only meant for the ordinary proxied-upload path, so keep it narrow whenever a new Azure error code is considered for fallback.
applies: Error handling for Azure Blob multipart upload setup, specifically which Azure responses from the delegation-key request trigger the proxied-upload fallback.
says: Azure authentication failures are hidden because large artifact uploads silently switch to proxy.
Surface actual Azure permission errors instead of silently routing uploads through proxy.
Invalid credentials cause slow proxied uploads instead of showing the Azure access error.
Report network policy rejections immediately when uploading model artifacts to Azure storage.
Users cannot diagnose Azure authorization problems because upload error messages are suppressed.
search: During Azure Blob multipart upload setup in `AzureBlobArtifactRepository.create_multipart_upload`, `HttpResponseError` from `get_user_delegation_key` is converted to `_UnsupportedMultipartUploadException` only when status is 403 and error code is `AuthorizationPermissionMismatch`. All other HTTP errors, including 403 status for `AuthenticationFailed` and `AuthorizationFailure`, are re-raised unchanged so underlying authentication, account, and network-policy errors do not silently trigger the proxy fallback. Transient errors, throttling (429), and authentication failures must propagate to the caller.
